headings.text: Product flavors: pick the right one

blocks.html:
A plugin is built with Gradle through the atak-gradle-takdev plugin, signed, and installed as an APK onto a device that already has a matching ATAK build.

The build setup

The top-level build.gradle applies the takdev plugin and declares the values that pin your plugin to an ATAK API:

buildscript {
    ext.PLUGIN_VERSION = "1.0"      // your plugin's version
    ext.ATAK_VERSION   = '5.6.0'    // the ATAK API you build against
    def takdevVersion  = '3.+'      // the atak-gradle-takdev plugin line
    // ...resolves the SDK from takrepo.url, or a local atak-gradle-takdev.jar
}

plugins {
    id("com.android.application")
}
apply {
    plugin("atak-takdev-plugin")
}

The module app/build.gradle sets the Android values — compileSdk 36, targetSdkVersion 34, minSdkVersion 21, and Java 17 — and its debug signing is preconfigured by the takdev plugin (see Set up your environment). It also names the output APK:

Product flavors: pick the right one

The 5.x example defines a compact set of flavors — **civ** (default), **mil**, and **gov** — generated from a supportedFlavors list. Each sets the manifest's plugin-api marker to the matching ATAK API:

def supportedFlavors = [
    [ name: 'civ', default: true ],
    [ name: 'mil' ],
    [ name: 'gov' ],
]
// for each flavor:
//   def pluginApiFlavor = flav.name.equals('gov') ? 'CIV' : flav.name.toUpperCase()
//   manifestPlaceholders = [atakApiVersion: "com.atakmap.app@" + ATAK_VERSION + ".${pluginApiFlavor}"]

For open-source development you build the **civ** flavor, because you install alongside ATAK-CIV (gov maps its API marker to CIV too). The plugin's API marker must match the ATAK build on the device or ATAK will refuse to load it.

ATAK 4.x shipped a much longer flavor list (fvey, aus, nzl, swe, …); 5.x's example trims it to civ/mil/gov. The build-task names below are unaffected.

Build & install commands

Gradle tasks combine the flavor and the build type (Debug / Release):

# Build a debug APK for the CIV variant
./gradlew assembleCivDebug

# Build AND install it onto the connected device/emulator
./gradlew installCivDebug

# Release build (minified + proguard, release signing key)
./gradlew assembleCivRelease

Substitute the flavor for other variants (assembleMilDebug, etc.). Debug builds are debuggable and skip minification; release builds run ProGuard (proguard-gradle.txt) and sign with your release key.

Run it

  1. Install the matching ATAK-CIV build on the device/emulator first. The plugin does nothing on its own — it loads into ATAK.
  2. ./gradlew installCivDebug to push the plugin APK.
  3. Launch ATAK. It enumerates installed plugin APKs (via the com.atakmap.app.component discovery hook) and, on first run, will typically prompt to load/enable the new plugin. Accept it.
  4. Your tool button appears in the toolbar; tapping it fires your SHOW_… action and your DropDown slides in.

Development-build watermark. Unkeyed developer builds of the host TAK app display a "Development Build" watermark across the map. That's expected for SDK development-tier ATAK and is unrelated to your plugin.

When the plugin won't load

  • API mismatch — the plugin's plugin-api marker doesn't match the running ATAK. Rebuild with the flavor/ATAK_VERSION that matches the installed app.
  • Signing — a release build can't find a signing key: configure your own release keystore (debug is signed automatically by the takdev plugin). See Packaging & distribution.
  • Not discovered — the com.atakmap.app.component activity/intent-filter is missing or the package was renamed inconsistently. Re-check the manifest and plugin.xml.
